title: Introduction Mans Purpose And The Declaration Of 2 Abysses

questions.question: According to the passage, why were human beings sent to this world?
questions.answer: To know their Creator, believe in Him, and worship Him.

questions.question: What does the passage say is the basic duty of every person?
questions.answer: To know Allah, believe in Him, and accept His oneness with full submission and certainty.

questions.question: Which two ideas about Allah are especially emphasized together?
questions.answer: His existence and His unity.

questions.question: Why does the passage connect human life in this world with worship?
questions.answer: Because worship is part of the main purpose for which people were created and sent here.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about human nature and its deepest desires?
questions.answer: People naturally want lasting life and endless existence.

questions.question: What other side of human life is mentioned besides hopes?
questions.answer: People also face many hardships and pains.

questions.question: Why are faith and knowing Allah described as especially important for human beings?
questions.answer: Because they are the foundation and key for eternal life.

questions.question: How does the passage judge goals and achievements that are separate from faith in Allah and knowing Him?
questions.answer: It says they are low in value, and sometimes not worth much at all.

questions.question: What can we infer about worldly success from this passage?
questions.answer: Worldly success alone is not enough if it is cut off from faith and knowing Allah.

questions.question: How does the passage connect certainty with belief?
questions.answer: It teaches that belief should include full confidence, not weak or unsure acceptance.

questions.question: What main message about the purpose of life appears in this passage?
questions.answer: The main purpose of life is to recognize Allah, believe in Him, and worship Him.

questions.question: In the passage, what comes first among human responsibilities?
questions.answer: Knowing and believing in Allah comes first.

questions.question: What does accepting Allah’s unity mean in this passage?
questions.answer: It means affirming that Allah is One and submitting to that truth with certainty.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the kind of life people long for?
questions.answer: It says people want a life that does not end.

questions.question: How are human hopes described?
questions.answer: They are shown as very wide and without limit.

questions.question: How are human troubles described?
questions.answer: They are shown as many and far-reaching.

questions.question: Why might a person need more than ordinary success or pleasure, according to the passage?
questions.answer: Because human beings want lasting life, and temporary things cannot fully answer that need.

questions.question: Which things are presented as the way to eternal life?
questions.answer: Belief in Allah, knowledge of Allah, and the means that lead to them.

questions.question: If something does not help a person gain faith or know Allah better, how is it viewed here?
questions.answer: It is viewed as having little value, and in some cases no real value.

questions.question: What lesson should a Muslim student take from this passage about setting priorities?
questions.answer: The first priority should be strengthening faith, knowing Allah, and living in worship of Him.

questions.question: What does the passage say is the wisdom behind human life in this world?
questions.answer: Its wisdom is that people come to know Allah, believe in Him, and worship Him.

questions.question: What word in the passage shows that this duty is not optional?
questions.answer: It presents it as an obligation.

questions.question: Besides belief, what attitude should a person have toward Allah’s oneness?
questions.answer: A person should accept it with surrender and firm certainty.

questions.question: What does the passage reveal about the human heart’s long-term wish?
questions.answer: It shows that people deeply want permanence and not to disappear.

questions.question: What tension in human life does the passage point out?
questions.answer: People have huge hopes, but they also go through many sufferings.

questions.question: What role does knowing Allah play in relation to eternal life?
questions.answer: It is one of the essential bases for reaching it.

questions.question: Why are other achievements described as small or even empty in many cases?
questions.answer: Because without faith and knowledge of Allah, they do not answer the greatest human need.

questions.question: Does the passage reject all accomplishments in life, or does it compare their value?
questions.answer: It compares their value and shows they are not truly great when separated from faith.

questions.question: What is one strong inference we can make about the meaning of a successful life from this passage?
questions.answer: A successful life is measured mainly by faith, knowing Allah, and worship, not just by worldly gains.

questions.question: According to the passage, what should a person understand first about his life in this world?
questions.answer: He should understand that he is here to know, believe in, and worship his Creator.

questions.question: What does the passage present as the first and most central human duty?
questions.answer: The first and most central duty is faith in Allah based on knowing Him.

questions.question: How complete should this faith be?
questions.answer: It should include submission and strong certainty.

questions.question: What does the passage say people naturally seek?
questions.answer: They naturally seek lasting life and endless existence.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention both hopes and hardships?
questions.answer: To show that human beings have deep needs and serious struggles that temporary things cannot solve.

questions.question: What are called the basis and key of eternal life?
questions.answer: Belief in Allah, knowledge of Allah, and the paths that lead to them.

questions.question: Which is more important in this passage: temporary accomplishments or what leads to eternal life?
questions.answer: What leads to eternal life is more important.

questions.question: How should a Muslim understand the phrase about other things being low in value?
questions.answer: It means they should not be treated as the highest goal if they are cut off from faith.

questions.question: What overall advice about life choices fits this passage best?
questions.answer: Choose goals that strengthen iman, help you know Allah better, and support worship.

questions.question: What is the central purpose of human life stated in the passage?
questions.answer: The central purpose is to recognize Allah, believe in Him, and worship Him.

questions.question: What does the passage say every person is required to do regarding Allah?
questions.answer: Every person must know Allah, believe in Him, and affirm His oneness.

questions.question: What kind of inner response should go along with this belief?
questions.answer: It should be joined with submission and complete certainty.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the human wish for the future?
questions.answer: It describes people as wanting a future that lasts forever.

questions.question: Why would temporary things fail to satisfy a person fully, based on this passage?
questions.answer: Because human beings want something lasting, while temporary things pass away.

questions.question: What three connected matters are treated as most precious here?
questions.answer: Belief in Allah, knowledge of Allah, and the means of reaching them.

questions.question: How are achievements without those three matters evaluated?
questions.answer: They are treated as inferior and often not truly worthwhile.

questions.question: What is the best summary of the passage in one sentence?
questions.answer: Human life finds its real purpose and value through faith in Allah, knowing Him, and worshipping Him.

questions.question: What reason does the passage give for human beings being in this world?
questions.answer: They are here to recognize their Creator, have faith in Him, and worship Him.

questions.question: What is identified as humanity’s original and binding duty?
questions.answer: To know Allah and believe in Him.

questions.question: What truth about Allah must be accepted along with belief in Him?
questions.answer: That He is One.

questions.question: How should that truth be accepted?
questions.answer: With surrender and sure conviction.

questions.question: What permanent wish is found in human nature, according to the passage?
questions.answer: The wish to continue forever and not come to an end.

questions.question: What problem in human life makes faith even more necessary?
questions.answer: People have endless hopes but also many sufferings.

questions.question: What is the relationship between faith and eternal life in this passage?
questions.answer: Faith is one of the main foundations for eternal life.

questions.question: What is the relationship between knowing Allah and eternal life in this passage?
questions.answer: Knowing Allah is one of the keys that opens the way to eternal life.

questions.question: Why are other pursuits sometimes called worthless here?
questions.answer: Because if they are separate from faith and knowledge of Allah, they do not meet the greatest need of human beings.

questions.question: What value system does this passage teach?
questions.answer: It teaches that the highest value belongs to iman, knowing Allah, and worship, while other things matter only after that.
